standard: Each dashboard claim receives three checks: source identity/existence, claim fidelity, and independent corroboration, arithmetic reproduction, or boundary challenge.

checks.evidence: University of California repository record, full One Earth article, authors, journal, and DOI 10.1016/j.oneear.2024.02.005 matched.
Summary directly states over 57 MMT produced/consumed in 2019 and less than 7% recovered for reuse.
Imports, exports, disposal, and stock arithmetic were inspected; EPA/CRS scope differences were retained rather than forced to match.
The peer-reviewed national MFA and DOI were verified at the institutional repository.
Results identify PP 8.6, HDPE 7.9, LLDPE 5.7, and PVC 5.2 MMT as the most-consumed individual resins.
Ordering and units were independently transcribed and checked; the four values were not misrepresented as the national total.
The same verified peer-reviewed MFA provides the application flow data.
Results report packaging 17.2 MMT and building/construction 8.3 MMT flowing into use.
Application values were boundary-checked against disposal values and labeled flows into use, not same-year waste.
EPA's current material-specific page and linked 2018 table were retrieved directly.
EPA reports 35.68 generated, 3.09 recycled, 5.62 combusted, and 26.97 landfilled, in million U.S. tons.
3.09 + 5.62 + 26.97 = 35.68; CRS independently warns EPA and OECD/plastics totals use different scopes.
National Academies report DOI 10.17226/26132 and full chapter were verified on the Academy site.
The assessment states the 1.13-2.24 MMT 2016 leakage range and the 914-species ingestion/entanglement count.
The leakage range was preserved as an estimate and the wildlife count was boundary-challenged so it is not presented as mortality or extinction.
NIST-hosted Argonne report ANL/ESIA-24/3 and DOI 10.2172/2315023 were verified.
Sections 2.3.1-2.3.5 directly describe feedstocks, monomers, and polymerization for PET, PE, PP, and PVC.
Pathways were cross-checked against the report's process diagrams and kept separate from product conversion and additive formulation.
Publisher article DOI 10.1016/j.resconrec.2023.107168 and matching 56-page supporting-information PDF were verified.
Figure S3 explicitly plots L/kg water consumption for PET, HDPE, and PP across four databases.
The source PDF was rendered and visually inspected; approximate minima, maxima, and means were independently transcribed and deliberately labeled figure-derived.
The peer-reviewed database comparison and NIST LCA review both exist and were retrieved from publisher/federal records.
Section 3.4 reports significant discrepancies and specifically discusses cooling-water recycling and database construction.
The NIST review independently confirms life-cycle studies vary in functional units, boundaries, data, and methods, supporting the no-silent-average guardrail.
The values trace to the verified journal supporting-information figure.
The calculation applies the figure's L/kg intensities to exactly 1,000,000 kg and preserves each range.
All liter and U.S.-gallon conversions are recomputed by the offline validator using 3.785411784 L/gal; replacement burdens are explicitly excluded.
The journal comparison, NIST review, and Federal LCA Commons portal were verified as real records/resources.
The sources document incompatible resin estimates and the need for explicit functional units and inventories rather than supplying a national replacement total.
A boundary audit found missing U.S. replacement mass ratios, wash cycles, losses, geography, and water-quality terms; the claim is therefore marked pending rather than assigned a number.
Current FDA page, WHO review, and EPA research page were retrieved from the issuing agencies.
FDA states current evidence does not demonstrate that levels detected in foods pose a human-health risk and identifies analytical limitations.
WHO and EPA independently identify method, exposure, and health-effect gaps; wording preserves uncertainty without declaring either safety or proven harm.
NEJM article, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2309822, methods, results, and limitations were verified.
The article reports adjusted HR 4.53 with 95% CI 2.00-10.27 for its composite endpoint among patients with detected plaque particles.
Study design was independently boundary-checked: selected surgical cohort, observational detection, unknown source/route, and no causal randomization; all limitations appear in dashboard text.
JAMA article DOI 10.1001/jama.2011.2034 and ATSDR PFAS health-effects page were verified.
Methods measured maternal and child serum PFCs and tetanus/diphtheria antibodies; they did not measure maternal microplastic ingestion.
ATSDR independently lists reduced antibody response to some vaccines among reported PFAS associations; the audit rejects both the wrong entity and the phrase vaccines did not take.
NTP monographs/profiles and NIOSH isocyanate guidance were retrieved from official federal sources.
NTP classifications support vinyl chloride, styrene, and acrylonitrile hazard statements; NIOSH supports irritation, sensitization, and occupational asthma for isocyanates.
Entity and route were challenged separately: monomer/reactive precursor hazard was not transferred to quantified consumer risk from every finished polymer product.
EPA research and TSCA compliance pages on fluorinated containers were retrieved directly.
EPA reports formation/leaching of eight PFAS from certain fluorination processes applied to HDPE containers.
The claim was narrowed to certain fluorinated HDPE processes and not generalized to nonfluorinated HDPE or every container.
Official European Commission, French ministry, German UBA, and Rwanda REMA pages were retrieved.
Each source documents a distinct mix of product restrictions, reuse/refill, deposits/collection, producer obligations, or exceptions.
Cross-jurisdiction comparison found continued plastic uses and scope limits in every case; plastic-free and realized-water-saving claims were rejected.
Official DOE Billion-Ton chapter and DOI 10.23720/BT2023/2316176 were verified.
Section 7.2.4 reports 0.38 Gt dry weight per year at <=$1,000/t using the 50% productive-area assumption.
The report's cost optimism, nutrient, siting, and engineering caveats were inspected; biomass was not equated with finished polymer or forecast output.
Official NOAA Fisheries seaweed-aquaculture page was retrieved.
NOAA reports more than 112,000 lb produced in Alaska in 2019 and describes the U.S. industry as developing.
The unit was audited as wet product and therefore prohibited from direct comparison with DOE dry-weight model outputs.
ACS article DOI 10.1021/acs.iecr.5c03802, abstract, process boundary, and publication record were verified.
The study reports substantial pretreatment/extraction wastewater and higher modeled water use than LDPE for its Saccharina film.
Pilot and prospective seaweed LCAs plus the technical review independently show formulation and scale dependence; the claim is kept to one case, not the entire material class.
Official UNEP roadmap and NIST plastics LCA review were verified.
UNEP prioritizes elimination of problematic/unnecessary uses, reuse, recycling, and reorientation/diversification; NIST requires functional-unit comparison.
The hierarchy was challenged against critical medical, food, infrastructure, and safety functions, producing staged validation and stop conditions rather than a blanket ban.
ACS Environmental Science & Technology article DOI 10.1021/acs.est.3c05191 was verified.
The paper reports plastics had lower greenhouse-gas impacts in 15 of 16 modeled applications.
Scope was challenged: the study is GHG-focused and cannot decide toxicity, water, litter, or biodiversity; it is used only to demonstrate burden shifting.
